q: If Particular persons members of a Corporate Town were lyable to answer for the Kings Debt before the time of their Encorporation, probably they continue lyable after the encorporation. Their Charters would not alter their case in this respect.
1726, Thomas Madox, Firma Burgi, Or an Historical Essay Concerning the Cities, Towns and Buroughs of England:
[…] all the solids by frequent swellings, pittings and relaxations are weakened, lyable to every descent of humors, […]
1734, William Stukeley, Of the Gout, page 78:
Talus, that could like a lime-hound winde her, […] At length found out whereas she hidden lay / Under an heape of gold.
1596, Edmund Spenser, “Book V, Canto II”, in The Faerie Queene. […], London: […] [John Wolfe] for William Ponsonbie, →OCLC:

My Hound then in my Lyam, I by the Woodmans art
Forecast, where I may lodge the goodly Hie-palm'd Hart,
1630, Michael Drayton, The Muses Elizium, The Sixt Nimphall, page 60:
Bob Munchy, as a forlorn hope, once threw his clodding leister at a drowning man, floating down the Yarrow in a high flood, and hauled him out with the lyams unharmed.
